title: Jamaican Stew Peas
subtitle: Slow-cooked kidney beans in coconut milk with scotch bonnet and allspice
excerpt: Dried kidney beans cooked long and slow in coconut milk with scotch bonnet, thyme, and allspice. The beans go in thick and creamy. This is a Sunday dish in Jamaica and it takes time, but the result is worth every minute.
sourceNotes: A central dish in Jamaican Sunday cooking. Traditionally cooked with pig's tails for richness; this version is fully plant-based and built on dried kidney beans and coconut milk.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions with the cooking liquid. Defrost overnight and reheat gently, adding a splash of water if needed.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a large pot and check the liquid level every 30 minutes during cooking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes even better the next day. Make up to 2 days ahead and reheat gently on the hob.

content.text: Jamaican stew peas is a slow-cooked bean dish built on dried kidney beans, coconut milk, and whole scotch bonnet. Keep the scotch bonnet whole so you get fragrance and warmth without full heat. If you pierce it, the dish will be very hot.

items.prepNote: dried, soaked in cold water overnight

content.text: Drain and rinse the soaked beans. Put them in a large saucepan, cover with fresh cold water, and bring to the boil. Boil hard for 10 minutes. Drain and return to the pan.
Add the coconut milk and enough water to cover the beans by 5 cm. Add the onion, garlic, spring onions, whole scotch bonnet, thyme, allspice, and bay leaves.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a steady low simmer. Cook uncovered for 90 minutes, stirring every 20 minutes.
Keep the liquid topped up so the beans always sit in liquid. Add boiling water as needed during cooking.
After 90 minutes the beans should be very soft and the broth creamy. Remove the scotch bonnet, thyme sprigs, allspice berries, and bay leaves.
Use the back of a spoon to break some of the beans against the side of the pan. This thickens the broth naturally. Stir in the olive oil.
Season with salt and black pepper. Serve with plain rice or rice and peas.

items.symptom: The beans are still firm after 90 minutes.
items.cause: They were not soaked long enough, or they are very old.
items.fix: Keep cooking and add more water. Old beans can take up to 2 hours 30 minutes. Never add salt until the beans are fully soft.

items.symptom: The dish is too hot to eat.
items.cause: The scotch bonnet was pierced or broke apart during cooking.
items.fix: Handle it carefully and check it often. If it splits, remove it immediately and taste before serving.

items.symptom: The broth is thin and watery.
items.cause: Not enough beans were broken to thicken the liquid.
items.fix: Mash about a third of the beans against the side of the pan with the back of a spoon and stir well.
